question:
Problems \(15,\) \(16,\) and \(17\) all refer to the following:

Don’t Crowd The Isles

In the very center of the Irenic Sea lie the beautiful Nisos Isles. In \(1998\) the number of people on these islands is only \(200,\) but the population triples every \(25\) years. Queen Irene has decreed that there must be at least \(1.5\) square miles for every person living in the Isles. The total area of the Nisos Isles is \(24{,}900\) square miles.

Estimate the population of Nisos in the year \(2050.\)
solution:
For the intended rough estimate, assume growth is spread reasonably steadily through each \(25\)-year period, so that two additional years make only a modest difference.

From \(1998\) to \(2050\) is \(52\) years, close to two \(25\)-year periods. After those two periods, in \(2048\), the population is
\[
200\times3\times3=1800.
\]
Thus about \(2000\) people, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\), is the intended estimate.

The statement does not specify that within-period assumption. For example, suppose that in every \(25\)-year period the population increases by \(50\%\) after two years and doubles at the end. Each period still multiplies the population by \(1.5\times2=3\). This schedule gives \(1800\) people in \(2048\), followed by \(2700\) in \(2050\), which is closest to \(3000\), choice E. Consequently, D is conditional on the intended growth interpretation, rather than forced by the stated rule alone.

edges.reason: The table rhymes improve speed for some multiples. The actual concept and calculation can use repeated equal groups, even for factors 7/8/9, so Gemini overstates a memorized fact family as necessary.

Here a multiple means several copies of the same amount, and one criterion is writing it with multiplication. That is exactly the repeated equal-addend meaning of multiplication. Specific times-table facts are not needed.
edges.scope: expressing several times a quantity by multiplication

edges.reason: Repeated decimal addition motivates multiplication by an integer and supplies checks. Computing the integer product then placing the decimal point does not execute a decimal-addition algorithm.

The source explicitly first computes an integer product before replacing the decimal point. Multi-digit integer by one-digit products are a component in that scope; the claim does not make a column layout exclusive for every multiplication.
edges.scope: integer multiplication before placing the point

edges.reason: The percent criterion explicitly represents the multiplicative relation between two numbers. A hundredths fraction represents that same quotient comparison; avoiding formal ratio terminology does not remove the relation itself. Require only this shared meaning, not prior completion of ratio exercises or notation.
edges.scope: The quotient meaning of the multiplicative comparison between two quantities

edges.reason: The example illustrates an estimate, while the general purpose is not confined to summation. Approximate sums illustrate estimation but do not define all estimation tasks. A length estimate or a rough product estimate can teach the purpose without this addition procedure.
edges.scope: rounding-based approximate sums as one example
